title: RTI Application, Right to Information Act, 2005
body:
To,
The Public Information Officer,
[Name of the public authority, e.g. National Testing Agency]
[Office address]

Subject: Request for information under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005

Sir/Madam,

I, [Your full name], resident of [Your address], wish to seek the following information regarding [subject of the demand, e.g. the investigation into the exam paper leak dated ___]:

1. [Specific question one. Example: the date on which the leak was first reported to the authority]
2. [Specific question two. Example: copies of any internal audit or inquiry report prepared so far]
3. [Specific question three. Example: the names and designations of the committee constituted to investigate the matter]
4. [Add further specific, answerable questions. Vague requests are more likely to be rejected]

I am enclosing the prescribed fee of Rs. 10/- by [postal order, demand draft, or online payment, as applicable]. If I qualify for a fee exemption (e.g. Below Poverty Line), I am enclosing proof of the same.

Kindly provide the requested information within 30 days as mandated under the Act, or 48 hours if the information concerns the life or liberty of a person.

Thank you.

Yours faithfully,
[Your full name]
[Your contact number and email]
[Date]
guidance: Ask specific, factual questions: what, when, how many, copies of. Not opinions or why questions, which PIOs can lawfully decline.
One subject per application works best. File separate RTIs for unrelated demands.

Keep a copy and the fee receipt. If there is no reply in 30 days, or the reply is unsatisfactory, you can file a First Appeal with the same public authority, then a Second Appeal with the Central or State Information Commission.
This generator only prepares the letter text. Filing (by post or the online RTI portal) and the fee payment are separate steps for you to complete.
